result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers reorder the columns with Name first, align text left and numbers right, normalize salary with separators and a currency label, and replace the black borders with light row dividers. B edges ahead on sorting because it names a default sort (by Name) along with the arrow indicator and aria-sort, while A shows an indicator but never sets a default sort. A covers more ground overall, with empty states, density and mobile behavior, but those extras aren't in the rubric. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers fully cover all five rubric items: name-first ordering, alignment by data type, consistent salary formatting, lighter row dividers, and sortable headers with indicators. B is slightly better. It explains its column order more clearly, puts the currency in the header instead of every cell, and adds density, responsive-layout and empty-state guidance. A is also strong and adds a frozen Name column and a clear default sort, but its salary example ($102,501 vs $102,500.50) is a little muddled.
